headline: Acquisitions lift revenue, tariffs squeeze profit
summary_short: Q1 revenue rose to $745.6M, up 9.9% y/y and 3.4% q/q on acquisitions and favorable FX, but diluted EPS fell 29.1% y/y to $0.78 as tariff-driven cost pressure, acquisition integration costs and higher interest expense compressed margins.
summary_long: Revenue rose to $745.6M (+9.9% y/y) as acquisitions and $37.3M favorable FX offset a $21.7M organic volume decline from Americas tariffs, Middle East logistics disruption and lower Russia volumes; organic sales fell 1.9%. Gross profit grew 7.8% y/y but margin compressed on tariff pass-through and higher freight/material costs from Iran-driven oil prices. SG&A rose $33.6M on acquisitions and FX; interest expense rose $8.8M on Bridge Loan costs for the pending $1.45B Eddyfi deal. Net income fell 29.3% y/y to $47.6M; diluted EPS fell 29.1% to $0.78. ESAB issued $1.0B of 2031 senior notes in March, lifting cash to $1,004.8M and long-term debt to $2,032.4M. Dividend was $0.10/share (up from $0.08); no buybacks. No FY2026 guidance figures appear in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Acquisitions (Bavaria, DeltaP, Aktiv, EWM) added $42.8M and $37.3M of favorable FX offset a $12.6M organic decline driven by Americas tariffs, Middle East logistics disruption and lower Russia volumes, partly offset by $9.0M of pricing.
Growth driven by acquisitions and FX, partly offset by tariff-related cost increases; margin fell on Americas tariff pass-through and higher freight/material costs from Iran-conflict oil prices.
SG&A rose $33.6M on acquisitions, related transaction costs and FX impact, outpacing gross profit growth and compressing operating income despite higher revenue.

Decline reflects the SG&A and margin pressure above, plus higher restructuring charges tied to Americas margin initiatives and EWM integration, and $8.8M higher interest expense from Eddyfi bridge financing.
Total EPS ($0.78) sits below continuing-operations EPS ($0.82) because of a $2.6M discontinued-operations asbestos-related loss this quarter; the remaining decline tracks the net income drop.

Cash and long-term debt jumped after ESAB issued $1.0B of 5.625% 2031 senior notes in March, partly to pay down revolver borrowings and partly earmarked to help fund the pending $1.45B Eddyfi acquisition.

Q1 growth came from four bolt-on acquisitions and favorable FX, while organic volumes and margins were pressured by U.S. tariffs, Middle East logistics disruption and reduced Russia activity, leaving profit lower y/y.
